structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This is a regulatory communication from UltraTech Cement Limited dated 28th July, 2025, addressed to BSE Limited and The National Stock Exchange of India Limited, with listing references to the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and Singapore Exchange. It notifies the stock exchanges that the Notice of the 25th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and the Integrated and Sustainability Report 2024-25 are attached, in compliance with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulations 34(1) and 53(2). The documents are being dispatched electronically to members with registered email IDs via the Company, KFin Technologies Limited (Registrar and Transfer Agent), or Depository Participants. The AGM Notice and Integrated and Sustainability Report are also available on the Company's website. The letter is signed by Sanjeeb Kumar Chatterjee, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, and includes the Company's registered office and contact details.

structure.title: N O T I C E
structure.summary:
N O T I C E
NOTICE is hereby given that the Twenty-Fifth Annual General Meeting of UltraTech Cement Limited will be held on Tuesday, 19th August, 2025 at 3.00 p.m. (IST) through video conferencing (“VC”)/other audio-visual means (“OAVM”), to transact the items of business mentioned below.

structure.title: ORDINARY BUSINESS
structure.summary: The text outlines four ordinary business items for an Annual General Meeting: adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY ended March 31, 2025, along with directors' and auditors' reports; declaration of dividend at ₹77.50 per equity share (including GDRs) for FY 2024-25; re-appointment of Mr. Krishna Kishore Maheshwari as a Non-Executive Director liable to retire by rotation; and appointment of Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP as Joint Statutory Auditor for five years at ₹5 crores remuneration plus tax and expenses, with board authorization for implementation.

structure.title: SPECIAL BUSINESS
structure.summary: The section covers special business at an AGM: appointment of Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP as Joint Statutory Auditor for five years at ₹5 crores; appointment of M/s. Makarand M. Joshi & Co. as Secretarial Auditor for five years at ₹7.50 lakhs; ratification of Cost Auditors' remuneration for M/s. D. C. Dave & Co. and M/s. N. D. Birla & Co. at ₹26,50,000 each; appointment of Mr. V. Chandrasekaran as Independent Director for five years; and adoption of a new Memorandum of Association with updated Objects Clause, new sub-clauses for power plant business, and liability clause changes, alongside substitution of Companies Act references. It also includes alteration of Articles by adding Article 124A authorizing power plant operations, and board authorization to file E-Forms.

nodes.title: Special Business: Secretarial Auditor Appointment and Cost Auditor Remuneration Ratification
nodes.summary: The page covers two special business items: appointment of M/s. Makarand M. Joshi & Co. as Secretarial Auditor for five years (2025-2030) with remuneration and authorization to the Board, and ratification of remuneration for Cost Auditors M/s. D. C. Dave & Co. and M/s. N. D. Birla & Co. for FY 2025-26, along with authorization to the Board to implement the resolutions.

nodes.title: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT
nodes.summary: The text presents resolutions for an Annual General Meeting: appointment of Deloitte Haskins and Sells LLP as Joint Statutory Auditor for five years at ₹5 crores plus tax, with increment(s) as recommended; appointment of M/s. Makarand M. Joshi & Co. as Secretarial Auditor for five financial years at ₹7.50 lakhs plus tax; ratification of remuneration for Cost Auditors M/s. D. C. Dave & Co. and M/s. N. D. Birla & Co. at ₹26,50,000 each plus tax; appointment of Mr. V. Chandrasekaran as Independent Director for five years; and adoption of a new Memorandum of Association with changes to the Objects and Liability Clause, including insertion of a new sub-clause for power plant business. Each resolution includes authorizations for the Board to implement.

nodes.title: Special resolutions for director appointment and MOA adoption
nodes.summary: The text presents two special resolution items from a company document. Item 7 covers the appointment of Mr. V. Chandrasekaran as an Independent Director for a five-year term, detailing the legal provisions and his eligibility. It includes the resolution text and authorization for the Board to implement it. Item 8 covers the adoption of a new Memorandum of Association in line with the Companies Act, 2013, with specific changes to the Objects Clause, including restated headings and new sub-clauses for power plant business activities. The page ends with a company name and page number.

nodes.title: “RESOLVED THAT
nodes.summary: The text presents two special resolutions for an AGM: (1) appointing Mr. V. Chandrasekaran as an Independent Director for five years from August 13, 2025, to August 12, 2030, under the Companies Act, 2013, and SEBI Listing Regulations, with board authorization; and (2) adopting a new Memorandum of Association per Table A of Schedule I, including restating Objects Clause headings, inserting new sub-clauses 50–56 covering power plants, retail platforms, building materials, machinery, tools, research, and management services, deleting the Other Objects clause, and substituting the liability clause to limit member liability to unpaid share amounts.

nodes.title: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT
nodes.summary: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the words ‘Companies Act, 1956’ wherever appearing in the existing Memorandum of Association be substituted with the words ‘Companies Act, 2013’ and reference to various Sections of the Companies Act, 1956 in the existing Memorandum of Association be substituted with the reference to the corresponding Sections of the Companies Act, 2013.

nodes.title: Board Resolution Authorizing Power Plant Business and Articles Amendment
nodes.summary: The page contains board resolutions authorizing the Board of Directors to file necessary E-Forms with the Registrar of Companies and to take all acts to give effect to a resolution. It also includes Item no. 9 for alteration of the Articles of Association by special resolution, citing Sections 5 and 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014. The resolution approves adding new Article 124A, which authorizes the company to set up, operate, invest in, and develop various power plants (including electricity generation, co-generation, waste heat recovery, captive, hydel, solar, wind, solar-wind hybrid, nuclear, and conventional/non-conventional/renewable energy sources), transmission lines, and associated facilities, on its own or through joint ventures, special purpose vehicles, or cooperatives; to engage in electricity generation, supply, transmission, trading, energy storage, and power exchange participation, including trading renewable energy certificates and carbon certificates. It also authorizes dealing in related equipment and activities. A further resolution authorizes the Board to file E-Forms and take necessary steps. The page ends with an order by the Board, signed by Company Secretary Sanjeeb Kumar Chatterjee, with place and date, and identifies UltraTech Cement Limited.

structure.title: NOTES:
structure.summary: The notes cover: an explanatory statement under Section 102 for items 4-9, with items 5-9 as special business and details for director appointments and auditors; AGM held via VC/OAVM until September 30, 2025, with quorum counting and deemed venue at the registered office; KFin providing e-voting and VC/OAVM facilities; proxy appointment not applicable due to virtual AGM; inspection of registers and certificates electronically from notice date to August 19, 2025; corporate members submitting board resolutions for representation; and no ratification required for the reappointed statutory auditor, Khimji Kunverji & Co. LLP.

structure.title: DISPATCH OF INTEGRATED AND SUSTAINABILITY REPORT, PROCESS FOR REGISTRATION OF EMAIL ID FOR OBTAINING COPY OF NOTICE AND INTEGRATED AND SUSTAINABILITY REPORT:
structure.summary: The text outlines the dispatch of the Notice and Integrated and Sustainability Report via email to members with registered email IDs with KFin or depositories. It mentions sending a letter with weblink and path to those without registered emails, per Regulation 36(1)(b). It provides weblinks for accessing the reports on the company, KFin, BSE, and NSE websites. It urges support for the Green Initiative.

structure.title: PROCEDURE FOR JOINING THE AGM THROUGH VC/OAVM:
structure.summary: The text outlines procedures for members to join the AGM via VC/OAVM, including login methods (e-voting credentials, OTP), device compatibility, and technical requirements (internet speed, microphone/webcam access). It details access timing (opens 30 minutes early) and first-come-first-serve participation, with exceptions for large members, promoters, institutional investors, directors, KMPs, committee chairpersons, and auditors. It encourages institutional members to participate and vote. It specifies speaker registration and query posting processes for members holding shares as of the cut-off date (12th August 2025), with deadlines and restrictions. Finally, it provides contact information for technical assistance.

structure.title: PROCEDURE FOR REMOTE E-VOTING AND VOTING DURING THE AGM:
structure.summary: The text outlines procedures for remote e-voting and voting during UltraTech Cement Limited's AGM, including participation via VC/OAVM and e-voting options. It specifies that e-voting during the AGM is for those who haven't voted remotely, and remote votes prevail if both are cast. It provides contact details for assistance, cites legal compliance, and details the remote e-voting period from August 15-18, 2025, with a cut-off date of August 12, 2025. Voting rights are proportional to shares held. It explains login credential acquisition for physical and non-individual shareholders, seamless e-voting for individual demat holders via Depositories, and advises updating mobile/email with DPs. Finally, it mentions three access processes: Depositories e-voting, KFin e-voting, and joining the AGM on KFin.

structure.title: A. Access to Depositories e-voting system in case of individual Members holding shares in demat mode.
structure.summary: This section details access to the depository e-voting system for individual members holding shares in demat mode for UltraTech Cement Limited's AGM. It covers login methods for existing IDeAS users via OTP or NSDL e-services, procedures for those not registered under IDeAS including NSDL and CDSL registration and login steps, and KFin e-voting processes for physical and non-individual members. It also addresses AGM access via KFin's VC/OAVM platform, e-voting instructions, eligibility, dividend payment and tax rules, IEPF transfer, general instructions on address changes, NRI updates, demat benefits, nomination, KYC, PAN, SEBI mandates, and special windows for re-lodging physical shares, plus helpdesk contacts.

nodes.title: 2. Existing Internet-based Demat Account Statement (“IDeAS”) facility Users:
nodes.summary: The text outlines access methods to the depository e-voting system for individual members holding shares in demat mode with NSDL. It details two login methods: OTP-based login via a specified URL requiring DP ID, Client ID, PAN, and verification code, with OTP sent to registered email/mobile, redirecting to NSDL's e-voting page and then to the e-voting service provider. Additionally, it describes the existing IDeAS facility login via NSDL's e-services website, navigating through Beneficial Owner login, accessing e-voting under Value Added Services, selecting the company (UltraTech Cement Limited) or ESP (KFin), and being redirected to KFin's website for voting.

nodes.title: 3. Those not registered under IDeAS:
nodes.summary: The text outlines e-voting procedures for UltraTech Cement Limited's AGM, covering registration and login for NSDL IDeAS portal, including steps for unregistered users, demat account holders, and mobile app use. It details CDSL login methods for Easi/Easiest users, direct e-voting access, and demat account login via Depository Participant. For KFin e-voting, it describes processes for physical and non-individual demat members with registered emails, including login, password change, voting, and confirmation. It also addresses members without registered emails, requiring ISR form submission, and provides helpdesk contacts for NSDL and CDSL technical issues.

nodes.title: C. Access to join the AGM on KFin system and to participate and vote thereat.
nodes.summary: The text covers AGM access via KFin's VC/OAVM platform, including login steps and e-voting credentials, and eligibility based on the record date. It details e-voting instructions, including obtaining user ID/password via SMS, email, or phone; appointment of a scrutinizer; and e-voting during the AGM. It outlines dividend record date, payment methods (NACH/NEFT), tax deduction, and IEPF transfer rules for unpaid dividends and shares. It provides general instructions on change of address, NRI updates, folio consolidation, demat benefits, nomination, KYC, PAN submission, and SEBI's demat mandate for service requests. It also describes the Senior Citizens Investor Cell, Online Personal Verification (OPV) process, and SEBI's special window for re-lodging physical share transfers.

structure.title: For ease of participation by Members, provided below are some key details regarding the AGM for your reference:
structure.summary: The text provides key details for UltraTech Cement Limited's AGM, including links for live webcast, VC/OAVM participation, query posting, speaker registration, and remote e-voting, along with usernames, passwords, and helpline numbers for VC and e-voting. structure.title: Mr. Aditya Vikram Birla
structure.summary: The text covers the Aditya Birla Group's Chairman's message for FY 2024-25, highlighting resilience, growth, and strategic moves in new platforms like paints and jewellery retail, alongside core sectors. It discusses global economic trends, India's standout GDP growth, inflation, and policy responses. The Group's people-centric approach is detailed, including hiring, diversity, learning initiatives, and employee well-being. UltraTech Cement's performance is summarized, with capacity expansions, sustainability goals, and nation-building contributions. The document also includes UltraTech's corporate overview, ESG performance, financial highlights, and table of contents for the annual report.

structure.title: About the report
structure.summary: The text outlines the report's scope, covering UltraTech Cement's operations across India, Sri Lanka, the UAE, and Bahrain, including all manufacturing units, subsidiaries, and bulk terminals, with over 90% of operations included in environmental and social reporting. It lists covered subsidiaries, specifies the reporting period (April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025), and mentions evaluation by Commitment on 10. It describes strategies for generating value across six capitals through governance, cost minimization, training, research, and community collaboration, with effectiveness assessed via stakeholder feedback, audits, and global forums. It lists the six capitals impacted and alignment with UNSDGs. It covers feedback solicitation, targeted readers (stakeholders), a precautionary statement on environmental impact and EHS management, assurance by BDO India LLP (report on page 523), and registered office address and contact details.

structure.title: FY 2024-25 Highlights: Financial, Operational and Sustainability Metrics
structure.summary: The page presents FY 2024-25 highlights under 'Growing with purpose,' summarizing financial, operational, and sustainability metrics with comparisons to FY 2023-24 and FY 2022-23. Financial data include net revenue (₹75,955 crores), PAT (₹6,309 crores), and revenue growth of 7.1%. Operational metrics cover grey cement sales volume growth of 13.64%, grey cement production growth of 14.1%, grey cement sales (133.14 MMT), and grey cement production (131.64 MMT). Sustainability metrics include a 1.2% reduction in Scope 1 net CO2 emissions (549 kgCO2/t cementitious material) and a 26.36% increase in green energy mix (27.8%). All figures are shown across the three fiscal years.

structure.title: ESG Dashboard and Impact in Numbers FY 2024-25
structure.summary: The page presents an ESG dashboard with impact in numbers, offering a snapshot of environmental, social, and governance outcomes from FY 2024–25. It lists key ratings and scores: Climate Action B, CSA Score 73, Water Security B, CSA Rank 9 in DJSI Sector Construction Materials, Supplier Engagement Assessment B, ESG Score 57 (2023), ESG Rating B (2024), and NSE 62. Environmental focus areas include climate change mitigation–decarbonisation, green energy mix, and water positive, with targets and statuses such as 13% reduction in Scope 1 GHG intensity and 69% reduction in Scope 2 GHG intensity by 2032, SBTi commitment to net zero by 2050, 27.8% progress, 85% green energy mix by 2030, 100% RE by 2050, and 4.9x status. Social focus areas cover training hours per employee, women in workforce, LTIFR, and lives touched, with statuses 5X, 23.9, 5%, 0.21, and 1.8 million. Governance focus areas include 30% women on Board and 50% board independence, with status 15. The page is from UltraTech Cement Limited's Integrated and Sustainability Report 2024-25.

structure.title: Nation-building through scale and sustainability
structure.summary: The Managing Director's message covers UltraTech's role in India's growth, macroeconomic conditions including global and Indian GDP projections, and government infrastructure spending boosting cement demand. It details UltraTech's capacity expansion to 188.8 MTPA through acquisitions and organic growth, financial performance with net revenue of ₹75,955 crores and 14% sales volume growth, and strategic capex plans. Sustainability achievements include 1.02 GW renewable energy capacity, 46% green energy mix, reduced CO2 intensity, water positivity, and circular economy initiatives. It also discusses future plans like entering wires and cables and ongoing commitment to nation-building.

structure.title: UltraTech's FY 2024-25 Highlights: Growth, Sustainability, and Innovation
structure.summary: The page presents UltraTech Cement's 'Year in review' and 'Defining moments' for FY 2024-25, organized quarterly. Q1 highlights becoming India's largest cement manufacturer with two new units surpassing 150 MTPA grey cement production. Q2 covers strengthened international footprint via increased stake in Ras Al Khaimah Co. (making it a subsidiary) and $500 million sustainability-linked financing reaffirming ESG commitment. Q3 notes ranking No.1 in sustainability in India's Cement and Building Materials sector by BW Businessworld for the fourth consecutive time. Q4 details green logistics with 100 additional EV trucks, and collaboration with UCLA on ZeroCAL decarbonisation technology. Additionally, the page covers expansion through acquisition of Kesoram Industries' cement business (effective March 1, 2025) and India Cements (making it a subsidiary).

structure.title: A Force for Nation-building
structure.summary: The text outlines UltraTech's nation-building role in FY 2024-25, covering capacity expansion in key markets, strategic acquisitions of India Cements' assets and Kesoram Industries' cement business, and enhanced operational agility via digital integration and logistics efficiency. It also details sustainability efforts, including new WHRS and solar capacities, increased blended cement use, and improved energy efficiency, emphasizing balanced growth through green energy, circularity, and alternative fuels, all contributing to building a reliable future for India.

structure.title: Built for more
structure.summary: UltraTech Cement's FY 2024–25 growth included adding 16.3 MTPA of grey cement capacity, raising domestic capacity to 183.36 MTPA and total including overseas to 188.88 MTPA. Acquisitions of India Cements (14.45 MTPA) and Kesoram Industries' cement business (10.75 MTPA) expanded regional reach and synergies. A quote from Mr. Vivek Agrawal highlights last-mile reach, a paperless digitised logistics ecosystem, digital tools for channel partners, and high-quality products and solutions for home builders and large infrastructure projects, emphasizing nation-building and the idea that infrastructure value lies in its impact on people's lives.

structure.title: Sustainable by design
structure.summary: The text highlights UltraTech Cement's sustainable logistics initiatives: using 100% emission-free electric vehicles for clinker movement between integrated and grinding units; integrating EVs into local delivery fleets for last-mile journeys to cut air and noise pollution and carbon footprint in urban and semi-urban areas; and adopting river transport via National Waterway 1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system) for large-scale mineral gypsum shipment. These efforts are framed as part of a broader transition where sustainability is embedded in operational design, alongside green cement, circularity, and energy efficiency.

structure.title: UltraTech Cement: Overview, Vision, Mission, Strengths, and Strategy
structure.summary: The page profiles UltraTech Cement Limited, the Aditya Birla Group's cement flagship and a global building solutions leader outside China, with 183.36 MTPA cement capacity and 2.6 MTPA white cement and wall care capacity. It presents the vision to be the leader in building solutions and the mission to deliver superior stakeholder value through sustainability, innovation, empowerment, and customer centricity. It lists core strengths: fair and transparent leadership, experienced management, integrated operations, a leading brand, and an extensive distribution network. It outlines strategy across capacity and leadership, customer centricity, cost competitiveness, sustainability, and low capex with high ROCE. Finally, it highlights enhancing stakeholder value through top-quality products, sustainable value, customer experience, socially responsible and profitable growth, a premium brand, and strong financials.

structure.title: UltraTech's Manufacturing, Distribution Network, and Nationwide Reach
structure.summary: The page outlines UltraTech Cement's operational footprint, covering domestic and international manufacturing and distribution presence. It details a vast network of 37,000+ dealers, 1,08,000+ retailers, and 4,615 UBS outlets, emphasizing reliable service. Nationwide reach includes 50,000+ trucks, 30,000+ destinations, 25,000+ daily truck movements, 60+ daily rake movements, 1,350 warehouses, and 300+ railheads. International capacity in Bahrain (1.0 MTPA), UAE (4.4 MTPA), and Sri Lanka (1.5 MTPA) is noted, along with regional capacity proportions across India (North 19.2%, West 18.2%, East 27.5%, South 18.1%, Central 17.0%). Facility types include integrated units, grinding units, bulk terminals, jetties, and white cement.

structure.title: UltraTech Product Portfolio and Sustainable Building Solutions
structure.summary: The page presents UltraTech's product portfolio, covering conventional grey cement (OPC, PPC, PPC Super, composite, Weather Plus, slag), white cement and putty, and ready-mix concrete with 27 specialty concretes. It highlights Greenvantage GreenPro-certified products for waterproofing, binders, plaster, grouts, repair, and flooring. Enviroplus concrete variants (Supreme, Enhanced, Classic) reduce embodied CO2 by 30–50% and achieve early strength. The Very Amazing Concrete range includes FreeFlow+, LiteCon, Pervious, Zip, Aquaseal, Rapid, and Thermocon. Contemporary sections cover UltraTech's retail chain (4,615 outlets across 23 states, mostly rural/Tier 3) and re-engineered dry mix mortars and waterproofing products.

structure.title: Value Creation Model: Capitals, Activities, Outputs, and Outcomes
structure.summary: The page outlines the value creation model, covering inputs across six capitals: financial (debt, equity, capex), manufactured (cement capacity, units), intellectual (R&D, patents, innovations), human (employees, training), natural (renewable energy, clinker factors), and social/relationship (CSR spend). It states the vision to be the leader in building solutions and lists activities (marketing, distribution, sales, building solutions) and associate functions (finance, HR, technical services, logistics, procurement, IT, legal). Outputs include cement sales, blended cement contribution, CO2 emissions (Scope 1, 2, 3), and product categories (conventional, contemporary, Greenvantage). Outcomes report financial metrics (revenue growth, EBITDA margin, ROE), manufactured (capacity utilisation, bags produced), intellectual (patents granted, new products), human (injury rate, fatalities, retention), natural (emission reduction, thermal substitution), and social (complaints resolved, MSME sourcing, community beneficiaries).

structure.title: Strategic direction
structure.summary: The text outlines the Board of Directors' strategic direction, emphasizing diverse expertise, independence, and governance. It details the single-tier board composition of ten members: a Non-Executive Chairman, Managing Director, Whole-time Director & CMO, five Independent Directors, and two Non-Executive Directors. Individual director profiles include names, roles, committee memberships, areas of expertise, tenure, and meeting attendance percentages. It also lists board committees such as Nomination, Remuneration and Compensation, Corporate Social Responsibility, Audit, Finance, Risk Management and Sustainability, and Stakeholders Relationship. A footnote indicates the information is as of March 31, 2025.

structure.title: Management team
structure.summary: The text covers two sections: a management team listing with names and titles of senior leaders, and an awards and recognition section highlighting external validations of performance, innovation, and sustainability. It details specific awards: UltraTech's win at the first RECEIC global symposium, recognition at e4m Pitch Top 50 Brands 2024, over 60 awards in FY 2024-25, Brand of the Year at ET Brand Equity DigiPlus Awards 2024 with multiple trophies, success at I-COM Data Creativity Awards 2025, and 16 trophies at the Advertising Club EMVIES 2025 for various campaigns.

structure.title: India's Cement Industry: Megatrends, Growth Enablers, and Sustainability
key_items: Megatrends and opportunities; What’s driving the future; Quantifying India’s development journey
structure.summary: The page covers India's cement industry outlook, highlighting megatrends and opportunities driven by GDP growth, low per capita consumption, and government policies. It quantifies India's development journey through economic growth projections, cement demand forecasts, demographic dividend, and digitization. Growth enablers include urbanization, housing sector expansion, and infrastructure investments. Sustainability is addressed through the industry's decarbonization imperative and UltraTech's response, including its Net Zero concrete commitment, green products, and concrete's versatile, high-performing, and resilient properties.

structure.title: UltraTech Cement FY 2024-25 Financial, Balance Sheet, and Operational Performance
structure.summary: This page presents UltraTech Cement's FY 2024-25 performance across financial, balance sheet, and operational metrics. It opens with a statement on consistent performance driven by strategic execution and market resilience. The Profit and Loss section includes five-year data for net revenue, EBITDA, EBITDA per tonne, normalized EPS, normalized PAT after minority interest, and book value. The Balance Sheet section covers capital employed, ROE (excluding goodwill), net debt/equity, net debt/EBITDA, and ROCE (excluding goodwill). The Operational section details production (clinker and cement in MMT) and grey cement sales volume, each with five-year trends.

structure.title: UltraTech Strategic Priorities and Roadmap for Growth
structure.summary: The page outlines UltraTech Cement's strategic priorities and roadmap, anchored in scale, innovation, and sustainability for resilient growth. It details six priorities: capacity and leadership (expanding production with ₹32,400 crores capex and 42.6 MTPA added), sustainability (low-carbon cement, alternative fuels, 67.9% clinker factor, 5.7% TSR), customer centricity (enhanced reach, new terminals, lead distance reduced to 384 km), low capex and high ROCE (prioritizing returns, 11% ROCE), cost competitiveness (lowest production cost, ₹86 per tonne savings), and integrated innovation and stakeholder value. Each includes focus areas, highlights, progress in FY 2024-25, capitals aligned (financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, natural, social), and UNSDGs alignment. The roadmap ahead emphasizes strengthening financials and ESG performance.

structure.title: Shared perspectives
structure.summary: The text outlines stakeholder engagement principles—shared perspectives, collaborative, inclusive, informative—and a proactive, responsive approach with descriptive, interactive, proactive elements. It discusses engagement with three stakeholder groups: industry associations, shareholders/lenders/investors, and government/regulatory authorities. For each group, it details need for engagement, importance of relationship, engagement platforms, frequency, and value created, including specific platforms like meetings, reports, associations (e.g., GCCA, CII), and rating indices, with frequencies ranging from monthly to annually.

structure.title: Stakeholder Engagement: Employees, Customers, Suppliers, Community, Media, NGOs
structure.summary: The page covers stakeholder engagement across five groups: Employees (ongoing engagement for high performance, platforms like health checkups, surveys, townhalls, CXO connect, appraisals; value: technological upskilling, employment equity, gender equality); Customers (educating on product value, mutually beneficial partnerships via website, campaigns, NPS, feedback, dealer meets; value: innovative solutions); Suppliers and contractors (responsible engagement per code of conduct, platforms like inspections, review meetings, vendor meets, grievance mechanism, ESG training; value: ethical sourcing); Community (supporting local communities, CSR, needs assessments, disaster workshops, satisfaction surveys, impact studies, grievance redressal, mason training; value: positive impact and social investment); Media and NGOs (understanding views, sharing management perspectives via one-on-one interactions, direct contact, social surveys; value: NGO collaboration and media awareness on sustainability). Each section details need for engagement, importance of relationship, platforms, frequency, and value created.

structure.title: Two lenses, unified focus
structure.summary: UltraTech adopted a Double Materiality process in FY 2023-24, aligning with GRI, SASB, IR, and ESRS standards and integrating with Enterprise Risk Management. The approach evaluates both financial materiality (environmental and social impacts on business performance) and impact materiality (business effects on environment and society), verified by third-party assurance. The methodology includes understanding operations and value chains, identifying impacts, risks, and opportunities (IROs) through research and stakeholder engagement, assessing financial and impact materiality with defined thresholds, and determining material IROs for disclosure. Outcomes include identification of IROs from services and value chain, insights on stakeholder materiality, refined scores mapped to ESRS subtopics, and a list of material IROs mapped to UltraTech’s specific matters. Results were presented to senior management to integrate actions, and stakeholder engagement was broadened to align strategic initiatives and maximize impact.

structure.summary: The page covers FY 2024-25 social initiatives: ensuring safe drinking water through new sources, refurbishment, ATMs, and solar facilities, impacting 1,10,000 lives; integrated child and women welfare via Anganwadi Excellence Initiative upgrading centers and establishing 102 model Anganwadis, benefiting children and women; Project Dhanvantari improving community health through camps, workshops, and medication; nutritional support to 742 TB patients with recovery success; and a success story of Ms. Ragini overcoming adversity through a waste management project, highlighting resilience and transformation.

structure.title: Fostering sustainable livelihoods
structure.summary: The text covers sustainable livelihood initiatives including Self-Help Groups, skills training, agriculture support, water conservation, and livestock improvement, benefiting over 181,055 annually. Case studies detail mushroom cultivation, the Bihan project for sustainable farming, sprinkler irrigation, organic farming, watershed development, HMV training, and Project Saksham for women's tailoring. It also addresses infrastructure development like road upgrades, solar streetlights, and Gokul Gaushalas for stray cattle. Business goals for 2025 in 300 villages include employment, income doubling, poverty reduction, farm productivity, and water positivity. Statistics on beneficiaries and outcomes are provided throughout.

structure.title: Community Development Initiatives: Water, Skills, Infrastructure, and Solar Energy
structure.summary: The page covers social initiatives: integrated watershed development in Malkhed and Tadipatri with check dams, percolation tanks, and rainwater harvesting, conserving 271 million litres and benefiting 36,122 farmers; HMV driving training for 30 youth in Kotputli, with 12 placed, recognized by the Chhattisgarh government and expanded to Manawar, also focusing on nutrition, wellness, immunization, and health infrastructure; Project Saksham bridging the gender gap by training 280 women in industrial tailoring, with 230 placed in textile industries; infrastructure development upgrading panchayat roads and enhancing accessibility for 552,432 beneficiaries, plus 10,000 benefiting from community halls; a case study on solar road lights in Chandrapalyam installing 24 solar streetlights, improving safety, economic activity, and reducing carbon footprint; and ESG performance goals by 2025 in 300 villages, including connectivity, road repairs, community halls, solar lights, water tanks, and piped water supply, with 44 of 507 villages slated to become model villages.

structure.title: Gokul Gaushala: A sustainable haven for stray cattle
structure.summary: The text covers UltraTech Cement's Gokul Gaushala initiative, which rehabilitates stray cattle by providing shelters with food, water, and veterinary care, converting waste to organic fertiliser, and has housed over 2,163 cattle, reducing crop damage and road accidents. It also details FY 2024-25 community initiatives, including infrastructure enhancements like cement concrete roads and community halls across 16 states to improve connectivity, quality of life, and resilience, supporting SDGs 9 and 8. Specifically, it highlights a community hall in Sondul and similar halls in other locations that host events, SHG meetings, and medical camps, fostering social cohesion and reducing financial burdens.

structure.title: Championing social welfare
structure.summary: The text covers social welfare initiatives including mass marriages, de-addiction awareness, gender equality and malaria eradication camps, and self-defence classes, benefiting 433,263 people. It highlights a case study of Project Parivartan, which addressed alcohol addiction in villagers through awareness drives, family counselling, and a 35-day rehab camp, resulting in reduced alcohol intake, increased workdays, and improved family income. It also mentions ESG performance goals for socio-economic empowerment of women through SHGs in 300 villages by 2025.

structure.title: Transforming Badanpur
structure.summary: The text covers UltraTech's CSR initiatives: transforming Badanpur village with education, healthcare, sanitation, water, and livelihood support, achieving 100% school enrolment and reduced malnutrition; rapid flood relief in Budawada, rebuilding roads and providing shelter; Project SAHAJ for menstrual hygiene awareness and eco-friendly pads in tribal Madhya Pradesh; and Milan Sangi Tihar Utsav, a women's empowerment event through athletics, now expanded to multiple locations. It highlights outcomes, participant numbers, and community impact across these social projects.

structure.title: Governance
structure.summary: This text covers ESG performance and governance at UltraTech Cement, detailing a governance framework built on accountability, fairness, and transparency, with Board oversight and alignment to UN SDGs, BRSR principles, and SASB standards. It includes a CFO message on financial performance, capacity growth, debt ratios, capex, and sustainability commitments. It outlines three governance focus areas: building trust through ethical leadership (Code of Conduct, anti-bribery, whistleblower policies), fortifying digital security (cybersecurity, tech transformation), and strengthening risk resilience. It also presents governance metrics, Board and committee structures, diversity (30% women), skillsets, meeting attendance, committee memberships, and an overview of relevant policies and guidelines.

structure.title: Shareholding pattern (%)
structure.summary: The text presents a shareholding pattern broken down by investor categories including promoters, banks/MFs/FIs, insurance companies, FPIs, government bodies, corporate bodies, foreign investors, individuals, GDRs, and employee welfare trusts. It also outlines the Code of Conduct, covering its application to the Managing Board and all employees, clear ethical expectations, regular internal audits for compliance and transparency. Additionally, it details the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy, emphasizing a zero-tolerance approach, preventive actions, applicability across all levels, legal compliance, and training for employees, business partners, and third parties. A 'FOCUS AREA' heading is also noted.

structure.title: Business ethics
structure.summary: The text covers business ethics and integrity, emphasizing transparency, ethical conduct, and long-term growth. It details compliance metrics: 100% directors trained in human rights and independent directors in familiarisation, and nil conflict of interest cases. Ethical pillars include employee code of conduct, anti-money laundering, whistleblower (with third-party confidentiality), grievance redressal via 'Xpedite' with escalation, anti-bribery, cybersecurity, and whistleblower protection policies. Code of Conduct pillars cover personal conduct, external interface, workplace conduct, and conflict of interest. Cybersecurity sections address multi-layered preparedness aligned with data privacy policy, DPDP Act gap assessment, consent management, nil cyber threats, 4,632 users trained, risk management, steering committee oversight, awareness programs, layered defence, and data protection. A CDIO message highlights digitalisation, AI, predictive analytics, and sustainability.

structure.title: Cybersecurity and Cyber Risk Management at UltraTech
structure.summary: The page covers UltraTech's cybersecurity and cyber risk management. It details a multi-layered strategy aligned with the Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Policy, including third-party gap assessments under the DPDP Act, a phased action plan, and a finalized consent management tool. It reports zero cyber threats and 4,632 users trained in information security awareness. Cyber risk management emphasizes prevention and detection, overseen by a Steering Committee with senior leaders including CDIO and CISO. A multi-faceted approach uses advanced technologies for detection, monitoring, and control. An awareness programme includes continuous training, campaign-based learning, simulations, and communication tools. A layered defence system protects critical assets with real-time monitoring, expert reviews, and 24/7 surveillance. Data protection complies with regulations, using backups, intrusion alerts, infrastructure upgrades, and decoy solutions.

structure.title: Mr. Anand Laxshmivarahan R
structure.summary: The text outlines UltraTech's digital transformation strategy, covering AI, ML, and digital twins for operations, predictive maintenance, and logistics optimization. It details smart manufacturing, SAP S/4HANA upgrade, RMC Control Tower, and Industry 4.0 initiatives including IoT, robotics, and IT-OT integration with micro-segmentation. Sustainability efforts include smart energy management and emissions reduction. Customer experience is enhanced via digital platforms. Partner empowerment includes driver apps (Eye-to-Track, RMC Driver App), vendor portal, logistics control tower, real-time KPI dashboards, paperless credit, and online quotation workflows. Emphasizes tech-enabled growth, resilience, and future-readiness.

structure.title: Digital Technology Transformation and Smart Manufacturing Initiatives
key_items: Integration of IT and OT (Operational technology) networks
structure.summary: The page covers technology transformation for operational performance, safety, and efficiency, including tech-enabled growth via SAP S/4HANA, RMC Control Tower, and AI/IoT/Industry 4.0 scaling. It details digital foundation strengthening through cloud integration, IoT sensors, predictive maintenance, and asset utilization; Industry 4.0 smart manufacturing adoption with robotics and sensing for safety; IT-OT integration using micro-segmentation, dual firewalls, Industrial DMZ, and secure remote access per IEC-62443. It also covers partner empowerment via Eye-to-Track driver app, transport management for BPD, RMC driver app, and One-Vendor Portal; internal stakeholder empowerment through Logistics Control Tower and Lite, real-time KPI dashboards, paperless credit workflows, and online quotation approval workflows.

structure.title: Customer centricity
structure.summary: The text covers customer centricity, detailing efforts to enhance customer experience through on-site support, complaint resolution, and digital transformation. It highlights AI integration for intelligent automation and customer insights, and describes digital touchpoints like UltraTech Trade Connect and Customer Connect apps. It also discusses tracking customer satisfaction via NPS studies, grievance redressal processes, brand performance monitoring, and a case study on empowering dealers through the Trade Connect platform.

structure.title: Enhancing customer engagement and sales efficiency
structure.summary: The text covers two main areas: enhancing customer engagement through the OneCRM platform, which addresses fragmented interactions by providing a unified view, intelligent visit planning, lead management, and cross-selling, leading to improved productivity and satisfaction. It then details risk resilience and compliance management, including an independent risk structure, the Risk Management and Sustainability Committee's functions (framework review, risk analysis, mitigation planning), risk classification by timeframe, and the risk management process (identification, assessment, mitigation, review, integration into HR evaluations, and continuous training).

structure.title: Risk and Compliance Management and Risk Management Governance
structure.summary: The page covers risk and compliance management, detailing an independent risk management structure that integrates risk criteria into product development, performance reviews, and operations. It describes the Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (RMS Committee), led by an Independent Director, which reviews the Enterprise Risk Management Framework, analyzes risks, and plans mitigation. Risks are classified by timeframe: long-term strategic, short- to medium-term, and single-event. The risk management process includes identification, assessment, mitigation, review, and integration into HR evaluations. Risk training covers Code of Conduct, Health and Safety, Cybersecurity, Social and Environmental Responsibility, Legal Compliance, and Logistics Safety. It also mentions external agency reassessment and periodic reviews to ensure resilience and alignment with business environment.

structure.title: Risk classification
structure.summary: The text covers governance and risk classification, explaining that risks are categorized by likelihood and impact, then prioritized by the RMS Committee for mitigation. It details long-term strategic risks requiring continuous monitoring, short-to-medium-term risks needing targeted action, and single unpredictable high-impact events needing contingency planning. A key risks matrix maps probability versus impact across high, medium, and low levels for areas like mining, logistics, workforce, strategy, climate, and IT. It references further risk details in the Management Discussion and Analysis Report and lists document sections on financial highlights, corporate governance, shareholder information, and sustainability reports.

structure.title: Standalone Financial Highlights
structure.summary: The text presents standalone financial highlights for UltraTech Cement Limited across multiple years (FY2015-16 to FY2024-25). It covers production and sales quantities of grey cement (clinker and cement), profit and loss account details (revenue, operating expenses, operating profit, other income, EBITDA, depreciation, EBIT, interest, profit before tax, exceptional items, tax expenses, net profit, cash profit, proposed dividend), balance sheet items (net fixed assets, investments, liquid investments, net working capital, capital employed, net worth, equity share capital, reserves & surplus, loan funds, lease liability, deferred tax liabilities), and ratios & statistics (operating EBITDA margin, normalized net margin, interest cover, ROCE, current ratio, debt equity ratio, net debt/EBITDA, dividend per share, dividend payout, EPS, cash EPS, book value per share, number of equity shares). Footnotes explain restatements and tax impacts.

structure.title: Directors’ Report and Management Discussion and Analysis
structure.summary: Directors' Report and Management Discussion and Analysis for UltraTech Cement's 25th Annual Report covers global and Indian economic outlook, cement industry trends, and the company's performance. It details production, capacity utilization, sales volume, and financial performance (standalone and consolidated), including turnover, other income, operating profit, cost highlights, finance cost, tax, net profit, key financial ratios, and cash flow statement. It discusses dividend, transfer to reserves, credit rating, and significant corporate developments: acquisition of The India Cements Limited, Kesoram Industries' cement business, Star Cement stake, entry into wires and cables, and acquisition of Wonder WallCare. It also covers directors' responsibility statement, capital expenditure plan, corporate governance, employee stock option schemes, share capital, awards, and statutory compliance.

structure.title: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
structure.summary: The text covers the Directors’ Report and Management Discussion and Analysis, focusing on Research and Development (R&D) efforts for decarbonisation. It details R&D's role in developing low-carbon products, conserving resources, and improving product quality. Specific innovations include low-carbon concretes, self-curing concrete, C&D waste aggregates, geopolymer 3D printing concrete, and limestone calcined clay cement. It discusses process innovations for energy efficiency and CO2 reduction, and collaborations for decarbonisation technology with Innovandi, startups (EnviCore, Queens Carbon, NeoCrete), Coolbrook, and UCLA's ZeroCAL technology. It also mentions the company's use of recycled materials and water conservation achievements.

structure.title: Sustainability
structure.summary: The text covers the company's comprehensive sustainability strategy, including SBTi-validated targets to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emission intensity by 2032 and net-zero concrete by 2050 via GCCA. Decarbonisation initiatives include green energy, alternative fuels, and R&D for low-carbon products. It details waste processing at Maha Kumbh, RE100 progress (28% green energy), and EP100 achievement (doubled energy productivity). Circular economy efforts include 21.73% recycled materials and water positivity (4.9x). Biodiversity assessments at 24 units and product EPDs are noted. A sustainable supply chain program evaluates ESG risks for suppliers. The company won a circular business model award, ranks 8th in S&P Global DJSI, and maintains a CDP climate score of B.

structure.title: Digitalisation
structure.summary: The text outlines the company's digital transformation journey, focusing on advancing intelligence through AI, ML, Gen AI, computer vision, and IoT. It details customer-centric initiatives like UltraTech Trade Connect and Customer Connect, partner empowerment via Eye-to-Track, and internal stakeholder tools such as Logistics Control Tower, OneCRM, and an RMC Control Tower pilot. It also covers operational efficiency improvements, safety pilots, AI-enabled logistics, knowledge management, and the UKSC's growth, CMMI L3 certification, and plans for AI-based review and control tools to enhance scalability and ROCE.

It details employee strength and extensive safety initiatives, including governance structures, risk mitigation, safety standards revisions, training programs, behavioral safety observations, audits, and technology integration. It also outlines CSR activities, spending, and committee composition, and reports on subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associate companies, including the acquisition of RAKWCT.

It also details Corporate Social Responsibility, outlining the CSR Committee, policy, vision, focus areas, and a spend of ₹165.16 crores. Finally, it addresses Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures, and Associate Companies, listing entities, financial statement availability, and UCMEIL’s acquisition increasing its stake in RAKWCT to 66.34%, making it a subsidiary.

structure.summary: The text covers related party transactions, stating they are arm's length, ordinary course, non-material, approved by the Audit Committee, and details are in Note 40. It then details risk management, including the board-level RMS Committee's functions, risk classification, and an external agency's review. Key risks identified are: raw material availability (fly ash, gypsum, slag) with mitigation strategies; environmental compliance and sustainability targets, including technology and partnerships; cybersecurity threats and mitigation; logistics disruptions with multi-modal approach; talent retention and development strategies; and strategy/growth risks from competition and substitutes, with vertical integration, new products, and digital ecosystem strategies.

structure.title: Internal Control Systems and their Adequacy
structure.summary: The text covers internal control systems, noting their adequacy, policies for sound management, asset safekeeping, resource utilization, financial reliability, and compliance, with defined roles and periodic reviews. It addresses director retirement by rotation, specifically Mr. Krishna Kishore Maheshwari's re-appointment. It details Board meetings held eleven times with dates, and lists Board-level committees including Audit, NRC, Stakeholders Relationship, CSR, Risk Management and Sustainability, and Finance. It notes independent director Mrs. Sukanya Kripalu's term completion and the Board's appreciation. References to the Corporate Governance Report for further details are included.

structure.title: Directors
structure.summary: This Directors' Report covers risks in logistics agility, talent retention, and strategy/growth, detailing mitigation plans like multi-modal logistics, EV adoption, and talent development. It outlines internal control systems, board meetings and committees, independent director appointments and retirements, annual performance evaluation, remuneration policy, key managerial personnel, audit committee, vigil mechanism, significant regulatory orders (CCI appeals), and statutory auditors' appointment.

structure.title: Directors’ Report: Appointments, Evaluation, KMP, Audit Committee, Vigil Mechanism, Regulatory Orders
key_items: Significant and Material Orders Passed by the Regulators
structure.summary: The page covers NRC recommendations and Board approvals for appointing Dr. Vikas Balia and Mr. V. Chandrasekaran as Independent Directors, and Mr. Sunil Duggal’s non-reappointment. It details Independent Directors’ declarations, qualifications, and IICA data bank registration. It describes the annual performance evaluation process and outcomes for the Board, committees, and individual directors. It outlines the policy on appointment and remuneration of Directors and KMP, lists the KMP, and provides Audit Committee composition and invitees. It summarizes the vigil mechanism/whistleblower policy and significant regulatory orders, including CCI penalties, NCLAT and Supreme Court appeals, and deposit status with no provision made.

structure.title: Directors’ Report: Auditor Appointments, Disclosures, Cautionary Statement, and Acknowledgement
structure.summary: The page covers auditor appointments (statutory, cost, and secretarial auditors) with terms and recommendations, and confirms no fraud reported. It details compliance with secretarial standards, annual return availability, and various other disclosures including no material changes, no differential voting rights, no sweat equity, no insolvency proceedings, and POSH Act compliance with harassment complaint status. It includes a cautionary statement about forward-looking statements and risk factors, and an acknowledgement expressing gratitude to stakeholders, banks, governments, and employees.

structure.title: ANNEXURE I
structure.summary: The text covers UltraTech Cement Limited's Dividend Distribution Policy, including its introduction referencing SEBI regulations, objectives, target payout ratio of 25-40% of standalone profit after tax, factors considered for dividend payout, general retained earnings use, review, and disclosure requirements. It also includes an Independent Auditor's Certificate on Corporate Governance compliance for the year ended March 31, 2025, detailing management's and auditors' responsibilities, the opinion certifying compliance with SEBI Listing Regulations, and the auditor's signature.

structure.title: ANNEXURE III
structure.summary: The text comprises Annexure III, the Annual Report on CSR Activities of UltraTech Cement Limited, covering the CSR policy outline, scope, committee composition and meetings, website disclosures, impact assessment summary, financial details including profit, obligation, spending, unspent amounts, excess set-off, capital assets, and reasons for non-spending. It also includes an executive summary of the impact assessment report for FY 2022-23, detailing projects across 16 states in education, healthcare, livelihoods, infrastructure, and empowerment, with outcomes and awards. Additionally, Annexure IV, Form AOC-1, provides financial details of subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures, including shareholding, profits, assets, liabilities, and exchange rates.

structure.title: ANNEXURE V
structure.summary: The text is an annexure under the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, detailing energy conservation, technology absorption, and foreign exchange disclosures. It lists numerous energy-saving measures including real-time transformer monitoring, static var compensators, induction motor analysers, ACC mist cooling, RTV silicon coatings, energy-efficient valves and fans, high impulse transformers, WHRS installation, cermet dip tubes, harmonic filters, renewable energy use, and various process modifications. It reports a capital investment of ₹682.8 crores on energy conservation equipment. Technology absorption efforts include calciner modification, polyamine water treatment, dry type reactors, intelligent MCCs, digitalisation tools, and alternative fuel utilisation. Benefits derived include reduced specific energy consumption, environmental performance improvement, product quality enhancement, and R&D capability building. It also covers alternative energy sources, waste material utilisation, and compliance with the Energy Conservation Act and PAT scheme, including ESCerts trading.

structure.title: ANNEXURE VI
structure.summary: This statutory report annexure covers imported technology (nil), R&D expenditure details for 2024-25 and 2023-24 (in-house, capital, recurring, contributions, total, and % of turnover), and remuneration disclosures under Section 197(12) of the Companies Act, 2013. It lists percentage increases in remuneration and ratios to median remuneration for directors and key managerial personnel, including changes in directorship. It also provides median employee remuneration (₹7.78 lakhs), employee count (25,684), average salary increase (10.29% vs. managerial 18.29%), and affirms compliance with the Remuneration Policy. Signed by Chairman Kumar Mangalam Birla.

structure.title: Report on Corporate Governance
structure.summary: The Corporate Governance report covers UltraTech Cement's governance philosophy, emphasizing ethics, transparency, and ESG principles aligned with the Aditya Birla Group's values. It details board composition as of March 31, 2025, including director profiles, independence, diversity, and succession planning. It outlines the Code of Conduct, board meeting frequency, attendance, and evaluation processes. It describes six board committees—Audit, Stakeholders Relationship, Nomination and Remuneration, Risk Management and Sustainability, CSR, and Finance—their composition, meetings, and terms of reference. It covers employee stock option schemes, remuneration of directors, D&O insurance, and insider trading prevention. Disclosures include related party transactions, penalties, vigil mechanism, anti-money laundering, POSH Act compliance, auditor fees, discretionary requirements, and CEO/CFO certification. General body meetings, postal ballot voting, investor communication, and website disclosures are also summarized.

nodes.title: Company’s Philosophy on Corporate Governance
nodes.summary: The report outlines UltraTech Cement's corporate governance framework, divided into sections like philosophy, remuneration, disclosures, board and committees, policies, and shareholder information. It emphasizes ethical, transparent practices for stakeholder fairness and describes governance as mechanisms and relations for Board control. Core principles include transparency, accountability, and sustainability. Business decisions align with laws and integrate ESG principles. The 'Power of Five' values—Integrity, Passion, Speed, Commitment, and Seamlessness—are detailed and drive culture and excellence. The philosophy resonates with the Aditya Birla Group's purpose to enrich lives through responsible businesses that inspire trust. The text includes page numbers and document context.

structure.summary: This note details UltraTech Cement's acquisition of RAKWCT through its subsidiary UCMEIL. On July 10, 2024, UCMEIL acquired 25% of RAKWCT, increasing its aggregate shareholding to 54.79% and making RAKWCT a subsidiary. The acquisition was achieved in stages, resulting in remeasurement of previously held interest (gain of ₹18.91 crores) and transfer of accumulated OCI loss of ₹26.12 crores to retained earnings. On November 6, 2024, UCMEIL further acquired 11.55%, increasing shareholding to 66.34%, with ₹11.86 crores recognized in equity. The fair value of net assets acquired was ₹2,346.81 crores, resulting in goodwill of ₹529.24 crores. Non-controlling interest was measured at fair value at ₹968.02 crores. Acquired receivables had a gross contractual amount of ₹139.38 crores with no provisions. Acquisition-related costs of ₹6.42 crores were recognized. Since acquisition, RAKWCT contributed revenue of ₹489.53 crores and profit after tax of ₹46.77 crores. The acquisition aims to create operational efficiencies, synergies, and market presence in UAE and India.

A table details each risk: market risk (foreign currency, interest rate, commodity) with exposures, measurement methods (sensitivity analysis, cash flow forecasting), and management tools (forwards, swaps, diversification); credit risk with exposures (receivables, investments, derivatives) and management (credit monitoring, factoring); and liquidity risk with exposures (borrowings, liabilities) and management (credit lines, portfolio diversification).
